about: The one record of how Common Shade's knowledge has changed, for /growing/ ('Watch Common Shade grow'), llms-full.txt and the exit card. One entry per change, reviewed by hand; tools/growth-candidates.js proposes candidates and never publishes. 'added' is the day the change reached the site (its merged pull request, 'pr'); 'event' is the date of the underlying work, as printed by its source or computed from its records ('span'). 'why' is Common Shade's reading; 'finding' is what a source says, quoted from text already on the site (the check confirms it appears there). 'links' join an entry to records on the map: basis 'record' when the connection is in the site's structured data, 'editorial' when it is our reviewed mapping. 'effort' names the check files behind the change; the page counts them into 'What it took to add this' and never types a number. Kinds, places, people and topics come from fixed lists (see tools/growth-text.js). IDs are stable.

entries.title: COP31, third check-in: a cooling roadmap and WHO's El Niño plan
entries.why: Governments backed a voluntary roadmap on heat resilience and cooling at the Cooling Ministerial, with new support announced, and WHO set out its El Niño health plan. Each joins the watch on the step it has reached.
entries.review: Seven sources staged; five passed the GitHub check at UNEP, WHO and Mirage News; two Cool Coalition pages blocked the check and nothing rests on them

effort.asked: What has COP31 added on heat since the second check-in, confirmed at the source?
effort.open: Whether the closing decisions name heat, and when the cooling roadmap is launched.

links.why: The roadmap and its support are for sustainable cooling and heat resilience.

entries.title: Heat from field to factory: cotton, informal work and who can stop
entries.why: A new page follows cotton from field preparation and hand-picking through yards and ginning to the factory, keeping heat on people, heat on the crop and harm to livelihoods apart. It asks who can actually stop work in the heat, lists measures with who acts and who pays, and links both ways with Heat inside factories.

finding.text: nearly all sowed by hand and most weeded, while few operated irrigation or sprayed
source: Better Cotton Initiative (study by Ardis Research & Consultancy): Co-creating sustainable futures with women cotton farmers in Pakistan, 2025

entries.review: Twelve sources staged and checked on GitHub; 21 of 22 claims passed, and occupational guidance is reused from the factory heat batch. A news report on early picking in Sindh was blocked and left out; Better Cotton's Pakistan pages could not be read and are not used; no individuals are named.

effort.asked: Where does heat meet the people who grow, pick, move and gin cotton in Asia, and what makes protection usable for them?
effort.open: Any measured study of heat strain among cotton pickers, yard or gin workers in Asia; evaluations of shade, water or paid breaks in cotton; checked picking calendars by region.

links.why: The page sets out what heat-safe work needs in cotton fields, yards and gins, and who can provide it.

entries.title: Heat inside factories: sources, protection and an intervention library
entries.why: A new feature follows heat by task, place and time through a garment factory, explaining why two people in the same building can face very different heat. Its library of measures, from roofs and steam repair to paid breaks and buyer purchasing, gives each one's evidence type and limits, with a finder, comparison, worked examples and a worksheet for workers and managers.

finding.text: women's core temperature fell only with air conditioning
source: Smallcombe et al., The Lancet Planetary Health, 2025: sustainable cooling strategies for garment workers under simulated extreme heat, a randomised crossover trial

entries.review: Twenty sources staged and checked on GitHub; 42 of 57 claims passed. EU-OSHA's guidance reset the checker's connection on two runs, so its claims are held back and the records that rest only on it are marked as not yet confirmed. The garment trial is labelled a laboratory simulation throughout; field reports are labelled as reports, not evaluations.

effort.asked: What reduces heat for people working inside factories, and what does the evidence say about each measure?
effort.open: Independent before-and-after evaluations in operating garment factories; women's experiences of menstruation, menopause and protective-equipment fit in heat; EU-OSHA's guidance once the checker can reach it.

links.why: The intervention library sets out how heat-safe work is done inside factories, measure by measure.

entries.title: From what clinicians report to the guidance they can already use
entries.why: The clinicians' survey presented at COP31 now leads straight to India's own guidance on heat and pregnancy, published by the health ministry and UNFPA India in May 2026 for healthcare providers and community health workers. It sits beside the survey on Signals and Who is at risk, and among the guides for heat-safe pregnancy and newborn care.
entries.review: The guidance page passed the GitHub check in the gap-lens batch with every term found (its date, the heat-risk checklist, functional referral systems, breastfeeding); only those terms are described
action: See the guides for heat-safe pregnancy

links.why: The guidance is written for the people who deliver heat-safe pregnancy and newborn care.

entries.title: COP31, fourth check-in: what maternity and newborn clinicians report seeing
entries.why: A survey commissioned by Wellcome, presented at COP31, asked 1,000 clinicians in pregnancy and newborn care in five countries, India among them, what heat is doing to the women and babies they care for. It joins the watch as a finding, labelled as clinicians' reports rather than measured outcomes, and the pregnant women group on Who is at risk now carries it too.

finding.text: 98% said they had cared for a pregnant woman, and 99% for a baby, whose health they believed extreme heat had harmed
source: Wellcome, 2026: Extreme heat is putting pregnant women and their babies at risk (survey results and methodology)

entries.review: Three sources staged; all five claims passed the GitHub check at Wellcome's own pages and Down To Earth; the India-only figures and the remark on climate finance rest on Down To Earth's report of the briefing and are marked secondary; no individuals named

effort.asked: What does the clinicians' survey presented at COP31 establish, confirmed at the source?
effort.open: Wellcome's own India breakdown, and a UNFCCC document for the share of climate finance that goes to health.

links.why: Clinicians in pregnancy and newborn care report heat harming the women and babies they treat, and ask for training and resources.

entries.title: Heat today and the next three days on every city page
entries.why: Each city page now shows an estimated heat stress (WBGT) for now and a daily peak for four days, from forecast temperature and humidity, with the method's limits stated beside it and the official warning service one tap away.
entries.review: The method, its limits and the data sources each opened on GitHub with every term found; on the day of the check the estimate for Singapore read higher than every measured station, as the method's own caveats lead one to expect in cloud

effort.asked: How hot will it feel to work outdoors in this city today and over the next three days, and what is that based on?
effort.open: Whether a fuller method that also uses sun and wind can be added without a new service.

links.why: Rules for heat at work are usually set in WBGT, the measure the estimate approximates.

entries.title: Five more Indian cities, Kolkata first
entries.why: Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Bhubaneswar now have city pages: each with its heat plan status as a checked document shows it, the vicious cycles the evidence ties to it, today's heat-stress estimate and, where the city has no plan of its own, a link to its state's plans.
entries.review: 27 sources staged and opened on GitHub; 21 passed with every term found and only those are cited; six failed or were blocked and nothing rests on them

effort.asked: What is heat doing in India's big cities beyond Delhi, Mumbai and Ahmedabad, and what plans are in place?
effort.open: Whether Kolkata, Chennai and Hyderabad publish city heat action plans of their own.

links.why: Each new city's page records where its heat plan stands.

entries.title: Five more cities across Southeast Asia and Bangladesh, Ho Chi Minh City first
entries.why: Ho Chi Minh City, Chattogram, Surabaya, Quezon City and Chiang Mai now have city pages, each with its heat plan status as a checked document shows it, the vicious cycles the evidence ties to it and today's heat-stress estimate.
entries.review: 24 sources staged and opened on GitHub; 18 passed with every term found and only those are cited; six failed or were blocked and nothing rests on them

effort.asked: What is heat doing in big cities beyond the capitals, and what plans are in place?
effort.open: Whether Quezon City's heat action team publishes a city heat action plan, and whether Chiang Mai's haze plans come to cover heat.

links.why: Each new city's page records where its heat plan stands.

entries.title: A heat briefing on every city page, and districts side by side in five cities
entries.why: Every city page now says what a checked study finds heat costs there, or that no checked estimate has been found yet, and lists the actions that could break its vicious cycles by how soon they could act; Bangkok, Delhi, Jakarta, Phnom Penh and Ho Chi Minh City also show their districts side by side, from modelled residents and ages to mapped hospitals, built-up ground and park area, with each figure's limits beside it.

event.what: City briefing and district picture added

entries.review: District outlines, WorldPop, ESA WorldCover and OpenStreetMap read on GitHub by a job anyone can rerun; district areas add up to within half a percent of Bangkok's area; an independent review led to clinics being left out and stronger wording on modelled residents and park area

effort.asked: Inside a city, where do many people, and many older people, live with little park space, much built-up ground and few hospitals nearby?
effort.open: Hanoi is held back until its city and district outlines line up; which other cities have open outlines good enough to repeat this.

links.why: Built-up ground and park area are what cooler design changes.

entries.title: New signals from Asia on heat at work, and lessons on heat insurance on the map
entries.why: Signals now follow Singapore's mandatory heat measures, the Philippines' new heat stress and compensation guidelines, South Korea's first emergency heatwave warning, a survey of outdoor workers in Viet Nam and the World Bank's report on heat in South Asia's cities. Income protection on the map now notes two lessons from India's first heat insurance for informal women workers.
entries.review: Every source opened by a check on GitHub with its terms found, in the same batch as the policy brief

effort.asked: Which commitments and findings on heat at work in Asia could the site follow?
effort.open: Whether each commitment moves up the ladder.

links.why: Three of the new signals are rules for heat-safe work.
The new Watch for notes sit on income protection in heatwaves.

entries.title: Heat over time on the Bangkok and Kolkata pages
entries.why: The Bangkok and Kolkata pages now show how each city's own weather station record has changed since 1991: nights and days in the hottest tenth for that place, and the hottest day of each year, with a trend only where a test finds one and a regional model line beside it for context. Cities without a long enough station record show no trend.
entries.review: Daily station records read from NOAA on GitHub by a job anyone can rerun; years with too many missing days are left out as gaps; an independent review set the completeness rules and led to the regional model being shown only as background, because it leaves out the city's own heat

effort.asked: Has this city's own heat changed over the past thirty years, by a measure a reader can check?
effort.open: Which other cities have a station record complete enough to repeat this.

links.why: More warm nights and hot days are what early warning is planned around.

entries.title: Heat over time on every city page, with a check for changes at the station
entries.why: Every city page now carries Heat over time: from a weather station record near the centre where one is complete enough, and otherwise saying that no station record complete enough has been found yet. A new check compares each station with the regional model and withdraws a trend where the record shifts in a way that points to a change at the station, so a move or new instruments is not shown as a change in the weather.
entries.review: Daily station records read from NOAA on GitHub by a job anyone can rerun; an independent review set the check for changes at the station, and that check led to a correction on the Bangkok page

effort.asked: Which cities have a station record long and steady enough to show how their heat has changed?
effort.open: Records for Ahmedabad, Chattogram, Colombo, Dhaka, Kathmandu, Phnom Penh, Quezon City and Surabaya; whether national weather services publish longer series than NOAA holds.

links.why: More warm nights and hot days are what early warning is planned around.

entries.title: Signals now shows what the evidence confirms for each promise
entries.why: Each commitment on Signals is now tracked deliverable by deliverable, so an office, a research fund and a future plan no longer share one status, and every milestone names its sources, what each establishes and whether the site's source check confirmed it. Secondary reports and pages that only opened are shown as such, nothing missing is called failed, and a filtered view can be shared, saved, printed or downloaded.
entries.review: Every existing record re-described from its own text and the site's check records, with no new claims; an independent review of the tracking model; the edge cases tested on fixtures

effort.asked: For each promise on Signals, what does the evidence actually confirm, and what would show the next step?
effort.open: The original texts behind records that rest on secondary reports, and content checks for sources that have only been opened.

links.why: Several tracked rules concern heat at work, each now with its effective date and evidence.

entries.title: State of the field becomes a dated, sourced monthly briefing with an archive
entries.why: Each edition now makes one argument and states what it rests on, keeps apart when something happened and when Common Shade reviewed it, and shows for every claim its source, what that source establishes and what it does not. Editions keep what they said at publication, corrections are dated in the edition and on the corrections page, and each edition has a stable link, a print layout and a Markdown briefing.

event.what: State of the field rebuilt as dated editions

entries.review: The October edition re-described from its own checked records with no new claims, its first text kept unchanged; one correction found and logged; an independent review of the edition model; the rules tested on fixtures

effort.asked: What does a monthly briefing on heat need, so a reader can trust it, trace it and act on it?
effort.open: The Philippines advisory texts behind the November edition have not been located; the edition says so.

links.why: The October edition's opportunity concerns heat-safe work, with what the evidence supports and what the funding trace cannot see.

entries.title: How heat is reported: one explorer over both collections, with each reviewed article's reporting trail
entries.why: The page now explains how a multilingual pilot complicated its first reading, and lets readers find every article across countries, languages and collections, see what the review found in each, compare stories on the same protection and build a source-linked reporting question. Missing information reads not recorded or not assessed, never as a failure.

event.what: How heat is reported rebuilt around an explorer

entries.review: Every record and comparison drawn from the two existing collections with no new article coding; comparison quotes checked against the reviewed fields; two stories found in both collections now counted once

effort.asked: Does reporting on heat follow protection from a named responsibility, through money and delivery, to results?
effort.open: A speaker's review of each translated headline (the review sheet is published), a human second coder (a protocol is proposed, not scheduled), and the pilot's original codebook (working definitions as applied are published instead).

links.why: Two reviewed stories on heat insurance for informal women workers are compared side by side.

entries.title: Heat plans and the heatwave longer than any on record
entries.why: A 2026 modelling study, checked against its open full text, finds that some future heatwaves in India and Pakistan could outlast the region's recent record even with low emissions. The heat action plan action now carries that as something to watch for, and the learning agenda asks whether plans, budgets and cooling spaces could keep running through one.
entries.review: Three claims, each confirmed word for word in the Europe PMC full text after the publisher's pages blocked automated checks; no claim dropped

effort.asked: Could a heat plan sized to the worst heatwave in memory last through a longer one?
effort.open: Humid heat, nights and Southeast Asia, which the study does not cover.

links.why: A watch-out on plans sized to the worst heatwave in memory.

entries.title: Humid heat in Southeast Asia, beside the longer heatwaves
entries.why: A 2025 study measuring humid heat stress across Southeast Asia, checked against its open full text, projects that far more people could face a week or more of extreme humid heat, with 6 to 9 hours of severe heat stress a day in Myanmar, Thailand and Cambodia in peak months. It sits beside the study of longer heatwaves, which covers daily maximum temperature in India and Pakistan only.

event.what: Scientific Reports, 2025: widespread heat stress will become the norm in a warming Southeast Asia

entries.review: Three claims, each found word for word in the Europe PMC full text; a second candidate study had no open record and was not used

effort.asked: Does humid heat in Southeast Asia make heat last longer for the body than temperature alone shows?
effort.open: Whether heat plans in Southeast Asia trigger on humid heat measures, and how long the longest humid heatwaves could last.

links.why: A second watch-out, on humid heat in Southeast Asia.

entries.title: Actions chosen in Build protection now carry into a plan
entries.why: A reader chose paid rest breaks in Build protection, followed the link to Plan a response and found an empty plan. The actions now carry across and join whatever the plan already holds, without replacing any notes, and each line says which actions it came from.

event.what: Build protection and Plan a response joined up

entries.review: Tested in a browser: three actions carried across, notes typed, the evidence and finance pages visited, and the same three actions and notes found on return

links.why: Paid rest breaks, the action that showed the gap, now arrive in the plan under heat-safe work.

entries.title: The Heat Assembly: a game about who can use heat protection
entries.why: A shaded hall can be paid for and open, and still be out of reach for a porter who would lose a paid turn by leaving the queue. Played alone or around a table over four rounds of heat, the game makes funded, open and usable different things, shows each person's outcome without a score, and lets players replay one decision to see whose day changes.

event.what: The Heat Assembly published as a game for one person or a group

entries.review: Every path through the rules was walked: none reaches every break without someone losing money. A solo game and a shared-device game were played in a browser, with keyboard-only play, a narrow phone at 200% text and reduced motion checked

links.why: A break that costs a paid turn is the game's opening problem.

entries.title: The Philippines' heat advisories: two more checked reports, and the open question named
entries.why: Two news reports, checked word for word, add detail to the Philippines' October 2026 labour advisories on heat: duties that step up with the same four heat index levels the site already shows, and compensation for heat stroke, cramps and exhaustion, with other heat illnesses that may also qualify where the link to work is shown. The advisory texts themselves were not read, because the department's pages turn away automated checks, so the record still says so.

event.what: Labor Advisories No. 19 and No. 20, series of 2026

entries.review: Seven sources staged; two news reports opened with every term found; the department's own pages and one other report were blocked, and are listed as not read

effort.asked: Can the Philippines' heat advisories be checked against their own texts?
effort.open: The advisory texts: whether further illnesses are compensable now or under review, and whether the 2026 advisory replaces the 2023 one.

links.why: Employers' duties tied to public heat index levels.

entries.title: Dry soils and heat arriving together, from a daily global record
entries.why: A data set paper published in November 2026, checked against the publisher's open PDF, finds dry and hot conditions occurring together more often since 2000 in several hotspot regions, faster than either alone would suggest, with China's Yangtze River Basin rising from 10 to 21 events per grid square. The map's drying soils entry now carries it with its limits: a reanalysis estimate that leaves out irrigation and reports no country result for South or Southeast Asia.

event.what: Earth System Science Data, 2026: a daily global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes

entries.review: Eight terms, each found in the publisher's open PDF; three claims confirmed; what was held back is listed in the batch ledger

effort.asked: What does a new global record of dry soils and heat arriving together add for South and Southeast Asia?
effort.open: Country-level results for South and Southeast Asia, and how irrigated plains change the picture.

action: See drying soils on the map

entries.title: A daily heat data set covering the region, in the Heat Tool Finder
entries.why: The Heat Tool Finder now lists CHIRTS-ERA5 from the Climate Hazards Center, a quasi-global daily grid of maximum and minimum temperature, heat index and WBGT, checked against the provider's own page. It is listed as an estimate for analysts, not tested and not locally validated, with its licence not yet verified.

event.what: Climate Hazards Center: CHIRTS-ERA5 data set

entries.review: Nine terms found on the provider's page; the start year and the Heat Monitor were not found there and are left out; a blog finding on ERA5 reading cool in hot extremes is held until its address is supplied

effort.asked: Can a new daily heat data set help readers in South and Southeast Asia, and what does it claim about other data?
effort.open: Whether ERA5 reads cool in hot extremes in Southern Asia, from the blog once its address is in hand.

pages: CHIRTS-ERA5 in the Heat Tool Finder

entries.title: Heat-safe work: protections that workers cannot use
entries.why: Heat-safe work now carries a watch-out, checked against an Oxfam America post: in Hong Kong some outdoor cleaners given cooling vests were stopped from wearing them because the vests covered a company logo, and in Cambodia workers whose unions had bargained over heat exposure were better protected. Equipment and rules help only where workers have the room to use them.

event.what: Oxfam America, Politics of Poverty: the unequal burden of extreme heat at work

entries.review: Seven terms found on the post; two claims confirmed; the ILO exposure figure, an unlinked garment-brand study and examples outside the region are held back in the batch ledger

effort.asked: What does an advocacy post on heat at work add for workers in South and Southeast Asia?
effort.open: The Cambodia study itself, and whether Hong Kong's sensor and smartwatch alerts changed how often cleaners rested.

links.why: A watch-out: protections that workers are not able to use.

entries.title: The year's climate findings: India's April heat, early warnings and El Niño's health risks
entries.why: Two Signals records now carry more from WMO's State of the Climate Update 2026, checked against its press release: an estimated 146.5 million people in India exposed to extreme heat in an April 2026 heatwave, countries reporting multi-hazard early warning systems up from 56 in 2015 to 136 in 2025, and WHO's first classification of El Niño's anticipated health impacts as a health emergency.

event.what: WMO State of the Climate Update 2026, released as COP31 opened

entries.review: Eight terms found on WMO's press release; three claims confirmed; the Nepal glacier collapse, quotations and figures outside the heat focus are held back in the batch ledger

effort.asked: What in WMO's State of the Climate Update bears on heat in South and Southeast Asia beyond the headline temperature?
effort.open: How many people in Southeast Asia were exposed to extreme heat in 2026, and whether early warning systems reach people working outdoors.

links.why: Early warning systems reported by more countries.

entries.title: A drawing beside Heat-safe work: the cooling vest
entries.why: Heat-safe work on the actions page now has an illustrative drawing beside its watch-out: an outdoor cleaner sweeping in the heat puts on a cooling vest from its stand, then hangs it back up. It adds no new claim; the checked sentence and its source stay above it, and the drawing loads only when a reader presses play.
entries.review: Drawn to the checked watch-out only: no second figure, a blank badge, the heat easing only slightly; checked for broken poses and reduced motion

links.why: An illustrative drawing of its watch-out.

entries.title: Plan a response: save the whole plan as a file, and open it again
entries.why: A plan made on Plan a response can now be saved as a file with everything in it, owners, notes and money included, and a colleague can open that file in their own browser to keep working. Nothing is sent anywhere: the file stays with whoever saves it.
entries.review: A browser check saves a seeded plan, starts again, opens the file and finds every part back; a file that is not a saved plan is refused

links.why: A plan can pass between the people who sign it off.

entries.title: The heat network: 40 more organisations link to their own heat work
entries.why: Forty more organisations in the heat network now link to the page on their own site that shows their heat work, not just their homepage. Each link was opened on GitHub and held the word it rests on; six that did not open or did not hold it were left as they were.
entries.review: 46 candidate pages found on the organisations' own sites; 40 opened with their term found and were applied; the rest are listed with the reason in depth-dropped.json

effort.asked: Which organisations' links open only a homepage, and where is their heat work on their own site?
effort.open: The organisations still linked to a homepage, many of them sites that turn away automated checks.
